newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip with US bonds, forecasts mixed.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip with US bonds, forecasts mixed.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds edged down on Monday tracking weaker U.S. Treasuries, and dealers said a further decline was likely on profit-taking after last week's rise to new highs in some tranches.
They added dollar-denominated paper was unaffected by the mid-morning announcement that a new rouble worth 1,000 old ones would be introduced next year.
"(Russian) officials' assurances the redenomination would not harm investors or individuals were apparently so persuasive that we have not seen any moves," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
"Russian debt just edged down after Friday's drop in the U.S. Treasuries -- further decline is possible," a Sberbank dealer said.

The U.S. bonds eased on Friday after sharp upturns in U.S. non-farm payrolls and a strong National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) report sparked inflation worries among investors, analysts said.
The Sberbank dealer said the fall in MinFins could be broken somewhat by Friday's news Russia planned to announce the schedule for London Club debt rescheduling in late September.
But the ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said the market was looking downwards as profit-taking opportunities opened up on the record levels attained last week.
"The market feels that current levels are high. Given a possible further decline in (U.S.) Treasuries, it is a good reason for many to take profits after the rise," he said.
